name: Ironpass Electrical Maintenance Night Crew Kit
description:
The Ironpass night maintenance crew kit is what infrastructure looks like from the inside — functional, unglamorous, and built for crawl spaces and conduit tunnels. The primary layer is a flame-resistant synth-cotton work shirt in faded charcoal with a band collar and chest pockets sealed by magnetic closures rated for electromagnetic interference environments. An Ironpass Maintenance Division patch sits on the left shoulder in grey and yellow — a wrench over a lightning bolt — and a laminated crew ID badge clips to the right chest pocket. The shirt's rear yoke has a spinal rig channel: a vertical reinforced seam with snap-open access panels that accommodate external spinal augmentation hardware without compressing the rig's port nodes. Over it goes a high-visibility vest in safety yellow with 360-degree reflective silver tape striping and a radio holster on the right chest.

The trousers are Fenmark ToughSeam Electrician Pants in deep charcoal — arc-flash rated, with reinforced knees, a deep back pocket with snap closure for circuit documentation, and a built-in knee pad system. The belt is a wide nylon rigger belt with a grounded metal buckle. Footwear is the Penrose Weld Boot in matte black — dielectric sole, composite toe, ankle-high with a side zip for fast donning. A matte-finish hard hat in yellow with a mounted headlamp and a flip-down face shield completes the head protection. Work gloves in arc-rated synth-leather are tucked into the left cargo pocket. The kit is clean at shift start but by 0300 it carries the smell of ozone and tunnel damp.
functionality: Flame and arc-flash resistant primary layers, spinal rig channel with snap-open access panels for aug hardware, 360-degree hi-vis reflective banding, dielectric footwear for live electrical environments, integrated knee protection, radio holster, EM-rated magnetic pocket closures, headlamp and face shield hard hat system
what_it_says: Essential infrastructure labor — the kind of work that keeps the city's lights on and is rewarded with a night shift and a tunnel assignment. The spinal rig channel says Ironpass accommodates augmented workers, probably because the rigs make crew members faster and more precise in tight conduit runs. The laminated badge says they are accountable, trackable, and authorized to be in places most people never see.
worn_by: Circuit-tier utility workers with spinal augmentation
manufacturer: Ironpass Infrastructure Division — standard issue; Fenmark (trousers); Penrose (boots)
price_range: Φ 290–Φ 420 (partially subsidized by Ironpass; boots and trousers employee-purchased)
story_hooks: The maintenance crew's tunnel assignment puts them in a section of conduit that does not appear on any official Ironpass map — and the wiring inside does not match any known corponation standard.
A crew member's spinal rig has been recording environmental data from every tunnel access point for six months; someone wants that data, and someone else wants to make sure it never surfaces.
The laminated crew ID badge grants access to a sub-level that was supposed to be decommissioned — the badge system never got the update.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian night-shift uniform with high-visibility overlay. Reads as serious infrastructure worker — charcoal base layer anchored by neon-yellow safety vest with reflective striping. Silhouette is squared-off and built for motion through tight spaces, not form. Hard hat with integrated headlamp adds industrial authority.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso for layering and equipment access, articulated at shoulders for reach and climb. Trousers have a straight leg with reinforced stress points at knees. Overall impression is function-first, silhouette-second — nothing tailored, everything practical.
physical_description.primary_material: Flame-resistant synth-cotton blend (shirt), high-visibility woven polyester (vest), arc-flash rated cotton-blend twill (trousers), dielectric composite (boots), polycarbonate (hard hat)
physical_description.texture: Shirt has a soft worn matte finish with subtle flex weave. Vest is crisp and slightly stiff with woven reflective tape that catches light sharply. Trousers are tight-knit twill with reinforced knee panels. Boots are scuffed matte rubber with ribbed sole tread. Hard hat is textured polymer.
physical_description.color_scheme: Safety yellow and deep charcoal primary; 360-degree reflective silver striping on vest; grey and yellow crew patch (wrench + lightning bolt); matte black boots. Accent of raw metal (grounded buckle, headlamp brass ring).
physical_description.closures: Magnetic closures on chest pockets (rated for EMI environments), snap closures on back pocket and knee pads, side zip on boots for speed, standard button-fly trousers, nylon rigger belt with metal buckle, hard hat chin strap (industrial quick-release)
distinctive_features: Spinal rig channel — reinforced rear yoke seam with snap-open access panels for external augmentation hardware
Laminated crew ID badge clip on right chest
Ironpass Maintenance Division patch (wrench over lightning bolt) on left shoulder
Radio holster on right chest of vest
Mounted LED headlamp on hard hat with flip-down polycarbonate face shield
Deep back pocket with circuit documentation capacity
Arc-rated synth-leather work gloves (stored in cargo pocket)
Grounded metal buckle on belt (intentional electrical safety feature)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4: Working class essential infrastructure. Issued uniform signals stability and credential. Not salvage, not corpo luxury — employer-standard issue worn by people maintaining the grid.
physical_description.cultural_context: Night infrastructure maintenance crew. Wearer is electrician, rig technician, or conduit specialist operating in the ungoverned substrate of the GLMZ. Equipment suggests active spinal augmentation (rig porting). Presence of laminated crew ID indicates institutional affiliation — likely Ironpass Infrastructure Division or contracted subsidiary. Person wearing this crawls through 0300 tunnels and lives in electromagnetic fields.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine at shift start (0000 hours). By midshift (0300), carries accumulated tunnel damp, ozone smell, cable dust in chest pockets, minor scuffs on knees and shins. Vest reflective tape may show smudges. Hard hat visor possibly fogged. Overall still functional and maintained — this is a working uniform, not a fashion statement.

Charcoal flame-resistant work shirt with visible spinal rig channel seams visible at rear shoulder. High-visibility safety yellow vest with sharp silver reflective striping catches the beam of light. Deep charcoal arc-flash rated trousers with reinforced knees. Matte black dielectric boots with visible tread. Yellow hard hat with mounted LED headlamp creating a pool of light on tunnel infrastructure — exposed conduit, cables, metal piping. Crew ID badge clips to right chest. Gloved hands hold circuit documentation. Ozone haze and tunnel damp atmosphere. Shot from front-right angle showing equipment detail and industrial setting.
